clue.text: Spooner's gardening blade nicked body

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of word pairs, so the two words here trade their first sounds

parts.note: a hoe is the bladed tool for weeding
nicked is British slang for arrested, i.e. caught

explanation.surface: Someone's garden hoe has been stolen, or has cut into a body.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the starts of 'hoe caught' and you hear 'co-hort'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cohort is a group or band of people, as a body of soldiers or supporters is.

clue.text: Actor Merle serious about refusing lead

indicators.note: the word declines its leading letter, so the first letter goes

parts.note: sober as in grave and earnest
on means concerning, as in a talk on art

explanation.surface: An actor named Merle is too serious to take the lead role.
explanation.definitionFit: Merle Oberon was the Hollywood star of Wuthering Heights; the clue names her by first name and profession.

clue.text: Short note on a right-winger's scientific base

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: to note something is to observe it
taken as written
a Tory is a British Conservative, on the political right

explanation.surface: A brief message about a right-wing politician's research station.
explanation.definitionFit: An observatory is a building where astronomers make scientific observations, a research station.

clue.text: Rolling grass shows way to be followed

indicators.note: rolling over turns the word round, so it reads backwards

parts.note: oat is a cereal grass

explanation.surface: Grass being rolled shows the path to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Tao, in Chinese philosophy, is the Way, the path of right conduct to follow.

clue.text: 100 — too old for insurance policy?

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
overage means past the permitted age

explanation.surface: A centenarian asks whether they are too old to get insured.
explanation.definitionFit: Coverage is the protection an insurance policy gives, so the word can stand for the policy.

clue.text: Zulu occupies home rebuilt in Cape — one where Tees lives

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for Cape

indicators.note: the NATO letter occupies the rebuilt word, sitting inside it
rebuilt signals the word home is reconstructed in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
Zulu is Z in the NATO phonetic alphabet
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Zulu moves into a renovated house in the Cape, which is where the setter lives.
explanation.walkthrough: Tees is the setter, so his home is 'my home' in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Chez moi is French for 'at my house', the setter's own dwelling.

clue.text: Big shot touching up back-stabber

parts.note: a VIP is a very important person

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: re means concerning or touching on

explanation.surface: An important person cosying up to someone is really a traitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A viper is a treacherous person, named after the venomous snake.

clue.text: Boring routine — pity that's not finished!

indicators.note: a word not finished is missing its last letter

parts.note: ruth is an old word for pity, as in ruthless

explanation.surface: Someone groans about the daily grind, wishing it would end.
explanation.definitionFit: A rut is a dull fixed routine one is stuck in.

clue.text: Pest visibly envious and cunning

parts.note: green with envy
fly is British slang for sharp and crafty

explanation.surface: A pest who is openly jealous and sly.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenfly are aphids, small sap-sucking insects that damage garden plants.

clue.text: Some gent when sloshed gets shiner

indicators.note: sloshed means drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man who gets drunk ends up with a black eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shiner' looks like a black eye, but here it means something that shines.
explanation.definitionFit: A gemstone sparkles, so it is a shiner in the literal sense of a thing that shines.

clue.text: Instrument of Green Power absolute

parts.note: utter means complete, as in utter nonsense

explanation.surface: Something about absolute power for the Green party.
explanation.walkthrough: Green is capitalised to suggest the political party; it is the golf green.
explanation.definitionFit: A putter is the golf club used for rolling the ball across the green.

clue.text: Wholesale slaughter Republicans recalled with memory

indicators.note: called back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: the GOP, Grand Old Party, is the US Republican Party
ROM is read-only memory in a computer

explanation.surface: Republicans remember a massacre.
explanation.definitionFit: A pogrom is an organised massacre of a persecuted group.

clue.text: Charlie in Hearts goal upended prophet

indicators.note: Charlie goes in the reversed string
in a down clue, upended turns the word string upside down

parts.note: aim means target or goal
Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A player called Charlie scores for Hearts, the Scottish football club, and is acclaimed.
explanation.definitionFit: Micah is an Old Testament prophet with his own book.

clue.text: Sword-bearer's second relative crossing road

indicators.note: the relative goes across after the road, in sequence

parts.note: mo is a moment, as in 'half a mo'
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: A sword-bearer's brief relative crosses the road.
explanation.walkthrough: Penny Mordaunt carried the Sword of State at King Charles III's 2023 coronation.
explanation.definitionFit: The politician Penny Mordaunt famously bore the ceremonial sword at the coronation.

clue.text: Drink in Med? It's a cider brewed in sober group!

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: AA, Alcoholics Anonymous, helps people stay sober

indicators.note: brewed means the letters are concocted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cider is ordered in a Mediterranean bar among recovering drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink' is slang for the sea; the Adriatic is part of the Mediterranean. The fodder sits inside the group with no word saying so.
explanation.definitionFit: The drink is slang for the sea, and the Adriatic is an arm of the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Lorry carries Conservative enchantress, keeping Liberal in line

indicators.note: the lorry carries the Tory abbreviation inside it

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry, a British truck

indicators.note: the enchantress keeps the Liberal abbreviation within her name

parts.note: Circe is the sorceress of the Odyssey

explanation.surface: A truck carries a Tory sorceress who keeps a Liberal in check.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arctic Circle is a line of latitude round the globe.

clue.text: Swear duck's missing from dish

indicators.note: the duck is missing from the dish, so that letter goes

parts.note: a course is a dish in a meal
a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Someone swears because the duck is missing from their meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To curse is to use bad language.

clue.text: Bananas go dry inside chicken, creating gas

indicators.note: the reworked letters go inside the bird

parts.note: a hen is a chicken

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Stuffing a chicken with bananas makes for flatulence.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrogen is the lightest chemical element, a gas.

clue.text: Rough hooch in yard draws Penny in, causing neurosis

indicators.note: the jumble draws the penny inside it
with draws, in says the penny goes into the jumble
rough means roughly made, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Cheap liquor in the back yard costs a penny and causes anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypochondria is a neurotic anxiety about one's health.

clue.text: Subtle twist in Duncan Edwards's initiation?

indicators.note: a twist reworks the letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the start of the word, its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of the footballer's surname

explanation.surface: A twist in the debut of Duncan Edwards, the Manchester United footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuanced means having fine distinctions, subtle.

clue.text: Engaged in protecting cross, talisman against evil

indicators.note: the outer letters protect the cross by surrounding it

parts.note: at as in 'at work', engaged in it
a mule is a cross between a horse and donkey

explanation.surface: Someone engaged in protecting a crucifix, a charm against evil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a crucifix, matching the talisman; it is the hybrid animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a charm worn to ward off evil.

clue.text: Easily handled in vast, endlessly vague domain

indicators.note: the yare piece goes into the shortened word
without an end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: great means huge
yare is a sailing word for a boat that is easily handled

explanation.surface: Something easily handled within a vast, unending, vague territory.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey area is an ill-defined zone where rules are unclear.

clue.text: Breastfeeds regularly — that's admired

indicators.note: regular intervals means every other letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mother feeds her baby at regular hours, and is admired for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rated is an informal word for highly regarded.

clue.text: Tees full of booze after sending back a puzzle

indicators.note: the filled word is sent back, read from right to left
the setter's word is filled with the drink

parts.note: the setter's own name, so me
gin is booze

explanation.surface: The setter, drunk, sends back a crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Independent the setter's pseudonym in a clue stands for the setter, so Tees means me; the reversal covers the filled word, and A is added after.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a mystery or riddle, something baffling to work out.

clue.text: Nasty gash in skin of aunt, stupefied with horror

indicators.note: the jumbled cut goes in the outer letters
the skin is the outside, the first and last letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: nasty reworks the letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A nasty cut on an aunt's skin leaves her horrified.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast means filled with horror or shock.

clue.text: Cut in contributions to the Treasury uncovered

indicators.note: uncovered strips the outer letters

parts.note: taxes are payments to the Treasury

explanation.surface: A cut in taxes is revealed.
explanation.definitionFit: To axe is to cut, as spending or jobs.

clue.text: Cold, is Tees only in loose underbodice?

parts.note: Tees is the setter, so 'is Tees?' becomes 'am I?'
sole means only

explanation.surface: The setter asks whether he is cold, wearing only a skimpy vest.
explanation.definitionFit: A camisole is a loose woman's undergarment for the upper body.

clue.text: Fairy queen married sailor

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A fairy queen marries a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Mab is the fairy queen in Mercutio's speech in Romeo and Juliet.

clue.text: Betrothed person's lovemaking halted around noon

indicators.note: it goes around the noon letter

parts.note: it is slang for sex
ended means stopped

explanation.surface: An engaged couple's passion stopped around midday.
explanation.definitionFit: One's intended is one's fiancé or fiancée.

clue.text: Scottish island, reportedly unknown, displays allure

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say it, so the island's name is taken by how it is heard

parts.note: Bute is an island in the Firth of Clyde
y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A rumoured Scottish island shows its charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Beauty is the attractiveness, charm, that draws people.
